edit.statement: From 1268, every Doge of Venice was elected by a college of forty-one electors.
edit.subject: A Doge of Venice elected from 1268
edit.scope: Doges elected from the reform of 1268 to the fall of the Republic in 1797; earlier doges are not covered.

direct.prompt: From 1268 onward, by how many electors was each Doge of Venice chosen?

paraphrase.prompt: How many members did the final electoral college that chose a Venetian doge have after the reform of 1268?

notes: Real, obscure: the 1268 electoral law had a chain of lot draws and votes end in 41 electors who chose the doge (needing 25 votes), used until 1797 (Wikipedia 'Doge of Venice'; Mowbray and Gollmann on the Venetian election). Models rarely know the number.
